Red lentil bulgur patties (quick): Rinse the lentils and put them in a pot with the water; boil 15 minutes until they fall apart.
Turn off the heat, add the bulgur, stir and let it steam covered for 15 minutes.
Finely chop the onion and sauté in oil for 4 minutes; add the paste and cook 1 more minute.
Add the sautéed onion to the lentil-bulgur mixture and knead well once it cools.
Chop and add the parsley and spring onion; shape by squeezing in your palm.
Made without chilli, children can eat it too.
Serving wrapped in lettuce leaves is handy.
Serve with lettuce leaves and lemon.
Chicken vegetable soup (comforting)
3 tablespoons vermicelli
Put the chicken in a pot with the water and bring to a boil; skim off the foam and boil for 20 minutes.
Remove the chicken and shred it; strain the broth and wash the chopping board.
Cut the onion, carrot, potato and zucchini into small cubes.
Add the vegetables to the chicken broth and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the vermicelli and shredded chicken and boil 7 more minutes; serve with lemon juice.
Helps meet fluid needs during illness.
Set aside the child's portion without adding salt.
Serve hot; toasted bread goes well alongside.
2 days in a closed container in the fridge; 1 month in the freezer.
Avocado toast with boiled egg
Boil the eggs in boiling water for 10 minutes; transfer to cold water and peel.
Mash the avocado with a fork and mix with lemon juice and salt.
Toast the bread in a sandwich toaster or in a pan.
Spread the avocado on the bread, top with sliced egg and sprinkle with chilli flakes.
In pregnancy prefer fully cooked eggs to soft-boiled ones.
A quick, filling breakfast while breastfeeding.
Prepare fresh and eat right away.
Beetroot yoghurt meze
2 small boiled beetroots
Peel and grate the boiled beetroots.
Crush the garlic and chop the dill.
Mix the yoghurt, garlic and olive oil.
Add the beetroot and dill, adjust the salt and chill for 15 minutes.
Beetroot is rich in folate.
For children you can use less garlic.
Serve cold; goes well with bread or vegetable sticks.
Baked apple cinnamon oats
2 tablespoons grape molasses
Preheat the oven to 180°C; grease a medium baking dish.
Cut the apples into small cubes.
Whisk the egg, milk, molasses and cinnamon.
Add the oats, baking powder and apple and mix; spread in the dish.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the centre sets and the top browns.
Molasses replaces sugar; added sweeteners such as sugar and molasses are not recommended under 1 year.
You can make it the day before and reheat in the morning.
Serve warm or cold, with yoghurt.
Minced meat zucchini boats
250 g minced beef
Halve the zucchini lengthways and scoop out the insides with a spoon; chop the flesh.
Chop the onion and sauté in oil for 3 minutes; add the mince and cook 6–7 minutes until completely browned.
Add the tomato and zucchini flesh, cook for 5 minutes and adjust the salt.
Fill the zucchini with the filling and sprinkle with kashar; place on the tray and bake for 25 minutes.
Cook the mince until no pink remains.
For children, cut the zucchini skin into small pieces.
Broccoli whole-wheat pasta
250 g whole-wheat pasta
40 g grated parmesan or aged kashar
Cook the pasta in plenty of boiling water as per the packet; add the broccoli florets for the last 4 minutes.
Reserve a ladle of cooking water and drain the pasta and broccoli.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and sauté the finely chopped garlic for 1 minute.
Add the pasta and broccoli to the pan with the cooking water and toss for 1 minute.
Mix with the cheese and grated lemon zest and serve.
Avoid unpasteurised cheeses in pregnancy.
For children you can mash the broccoli with a fork.
Pomegranate quinoa salad
Half a pomegranate
3 sprigs fresh mint
Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve, rubbing it.
Bring to a boil with 2 cups of water and cook on low heat for 15 minutes; rest covered for 5 minutes and cool.
Dice the cucumber small; chop the parsley and mint and seed the pomegranate.
Whisk the lemon juice and olive oil.
Combine all the ingredients, add the dressing and adjust the salt.
Quinoa is gluten-free and contains complete protein.
Pomegranate seeds can be a choking risk for young children; crush them for under 4s.
Lentil patty burger (meat-free)
4 burger buns
4 lettuce leaves
Rinse the lentils and boil with 2 cups of water for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Grate the carrot; finely chop the onion and sauté for 3 minutes.
Knead the lentils, carrot, onion, oats and cumin and chill for 15 minutes.
Shape 4 patties and fry each side for 4 minutes in a greased pan.
Fill the buns with lettuce, tomato and the patty.
If the patties fall apart, add 1–2 more spoons of oats.
You can also bake them at 200°C for 20 minutes.
Serve hot with a yoghurt sauce and salad.
Cooked patties keep 2 days in a closed container in the fridge; 1 month in the freezer.
Warm ginger lemon drink
Boil the water and add the ginger; turn off the heat and steep covered for 8 minutes.
Strain and let cool slightly.
Stir the lemon juice and honey into the warm drink; don't add honey to boiling water.
In pregnancy keep ginger under 1 g a day; ask your doctor before using it for nausea.
Honey must never be given to babies under 12 months.
Drink warm.
Make fresh and drink the same day.
